findings.citation: S. Majid, B. J. Schroers, "q-Deformation and Semidualisation in 3d Quantum Gravity", J. Phys. A 42, 425402 (2009), arXiv:0806.2587 (journal)
findings.summary: Under 'quantum Born reciprocity' (semidualisation), an operation that interchanges position and momentum, the irreducible representations of a 3d quantum-gravity model appear as 'monopole sections' (sections of Dirac monopole bundles) on fuzzy spheres in noncommutative momentum space.
findings.difference: The 'monopoles' are the bundles in which particle wavefunctions take values, not magnetically charged objects; no dark matter, no abundance, no electromagnetic charge. Same words as C2 (Born reciprocity, monopole, momentum space), different thing. Also a new finding of g2-monopoles/verify.json, written after known.json, with the same label; re-verified here.

quotes.text: The latter is an algebraic operation defined using quantum group methods that interchanges position and momentum.
a noncommutative Fourier transform gives us a picture of the irreps for this model as noncommutative monopole sections on fuzzy spheres in noncommutative momentum space

findings.citation: M. Onoda, G. Tatara, N. Nagaosa, "Anomalous Hall Effect and Skyrmion Number in Real- and Momentum-space", J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 73, 2624 (2004), arXiv:cond-mat/0405634 (journal)
findings.summary: Two mechanisms of the anomalous Hall effect, one set by the real-space skyrmion number of a spin texture and one by the momentum-space skyrmion density at the Fermi level, discussed as a duality between real and momentum spaces.
findings.difference: Topological textures of electron spin and band Berry curvature in a crystal, not solitons of a matter sector localized in momentum. A reader looking for 'topological objects in momentum space, dual to real space' (C2's p-localized solitons) meets it. Also a new finding of g2-monopoles/verify.json (written after known.json), same label.

quotes.text: the duality between real and momentum spaces
one is characterized by the real-space skyrmion-number, and the other by momentum-space skyrmion-density at the Fermi level

findings.citation: A. O. Barut, "Superselection rule for magnetic charges and the search for magnetic monopoles", Phys. Lett. B 38, 97 (1972), doi:10.1016/0370-2693(72)90749-6 (journal; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: Proposes that magnetic charges may occur only in superpositions |g> +- |-g> whose expected magnetic charge vanishes, states that 'cannot be split in electromagnetic interactions by energy measurements'; offered, as the title says, with the search for monopoles in view, and as testable.
findings.difference: Explains non-detection by the quantum state of the magnetic charge (zero mean charge), an 'another representation' explanation, not by localization in momentum or a conjugate sector; no dark matter.

quotes.text: the states which are superpositions of positive and negative magnetic charges, ∣ g 〉 ± ∣ - g 〉, in which the expectation value of the magnetic charge vanishes, cannot be split in electromagnetic interactions by energy measurements
The hypothesis that magnetic charges occur in the superpositions

findings.citation: B. Kursunoglu, "Gravitation and Magnetic Charge", Phys. Rev. D 9, 2723 (1974) (INSPIRE also lists Phys. Rev. D 12, 1850 (1975)), doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.9.2723 (journal; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: In Kursunoglu's generalized theory of gravitation every elementary particle has a magnetically neutral core holding magnetic charge in stratified layers of alternating sign, so that monopoles with a long-range field do not exist; the absence of magnetic currents from Maxwell's equations is attributed to their confinement in particle cores.
findings.difference: Magnetic charge confined inside every particle, in position space: a version of the record's second hiding option (binding into magnetically neutral composites, #11 §11.4), not a momentum-polarized sector; no dark matter in the abstract.

quotes.text: consists of a magnetically neutral core of matter containing a distribution of magnetic charge density in stratified layers of sharply decreasing magnitude and alternating signs so that magnetic monopoles associated with a long-range field do not exist

The asymmetry of Maxwell's equations with regard to the absence of a magnetic current can be understood because the neutral and charged magnetic currents and the neutral part of the electric current are localized in the core of the elementary particle.

findings.citation: J. Henderson, "The Nature of Dark Matter and Cosmological Structure Derived from Generalized Time and Spacetime Duality", Preprints.org (2025), doi:10.20944/preprints202509.1554.v1 (non-reviewed preprint)
findings.summary: A 'spacetime duality' and 'generalized time' cosmology: antimatter separates into a universe 'on the other side of the fabric of spacetime', five 'dark universes' coupled to ours only by gravity give the 5:1 ratio of dark to ordinary matter, and 'energy considerations preclude magnetic monopoles from becoming entrained in the flow of time in our universe'.
findings.difference: Monopoles are kept out of our universe's time flow, not localized in momentum; the abstract does not make them the dark matter; no Born reciprocity or position/momentum polarization. Non-reviewed, so no label above related. (Also a C1 lead: dark matter as gravitationally coupled dual universes.)

quotes.text: energy considerations preclude magnetic monopoles from becoming entrained in the flow of time in our universe

findings.citation: A. S. Goldhaber, "Magnetic monopole search, past and present", Physics Today 70(6), 12 (June 2017), letter, doi:10.1063/PT.3.3571 (magazine letter)
findings.summary: Argues that in QED or the Standard Model a monopole's magnetic charge cannot be spread out, since fractions of it would violate Dirac's quantization condition, and that by field energy the monopole radius should be at least an order of magnitude above its Compton wavelength.
findings.difference: Bears only on the hiding option of the shared-photon form, in which the analogs' field profile is spread wider than detectors (#11 §11.4): for magnetic charge of our own photon the charge itself cannot be smeared. Inference, not in the letter: a wide profile would need structure beyond QED and the Standard Model, such as a non-Abelian core. Silent on momentum-polarized matter; a short letter, not a calculation.

quotes.text: the monopole charge cannot be spread out because little bits of magnetic charge would violate the quantization condition

findings.citation: K. M. D. Hals, A. K. Nguyen, X. Waintal, A. Brataas, "Effective Magnetic Monopoles and Universal Conductance Fluctuations", Phys. Rev. Lett. 105, 207204 (2010), arXiv:1008.0269 (journal)
findings.summary: Opens by setting the absence of isolated magnetic poles, 'an old puzzle', against evidence for effective monopoles 'in the abstract momentum space' (band Berry curvature of ferromagnets), then proposes a conductance-fluctuation probe of them.
findings.difference: Berry-curvature monopoles of electron bands, not magnetic charges; the juxtaposition of the null result with 'monopoles in momentum space' is C3's wording, not its claim.

quotes.text: The observation of isolated positive and negative charges, but not isolated magnetic north and south poles, is an old puzzle. Instead, evidence of effective magnetic monopoles has been found in the abstract momentum space.

findings.citation: J. García-Moreno, V. Vento, "Electron and monopole properties in a dark matter model", arXiv:2610.02083 (2026; arXiv preprint only)
findings.summary: Extends Vento's two-photon QED (arXiv:2507.06697, on the known list as C4 partial) to the electroweak theory: the ordinary photon couples only to electric charges, an 'extraordinary' photon only to magnetic ones, and the new photon and the monopoles form the dark matter sector, joined to ours by kinetic mixing.
findings.difference: Dark matter made of magnetic charges under their own photon, the shape of C4's separate-photon form, but with no position/momentum polarization; one magnetic species against the electron, not an analog for each charged particle; couplings tied by the Schwinger condition with mixing, not fixed by reciprocity as an S-image. Same label as the earlier Vento paper, for consistency.

quotes.text: The new photon and the monopoles form the dark matter sector.
For simplicity we will consider ordinary matter to be made just of electrons and dark matter just of monopoles.
Here we generalize the Electroweak theory in the same way by incorporating a dark sector with massive photons and monopoles

findings.citation: M. K. Sullivan, D. Fryberger, "Proposal to Search for Magnetically Charged Particles with Magnetic Charge 1e", arXiv:1511.02200 (2015; arXiv preprint only)
findings.summary: Fryberger's composite model of Standard Model particles (magnetically bound vorton pairs) predicts a complete family of magnetically charged counterparts of the Standard Model particles, the lightest an electrically neutral stable lepton with magnetic charge 1e (the 'magneticon'); a search at the LHC is proposed.
findings.difference: A magnetic counterpart for every Standard Model particle, C4's first half, but in ordinary space and expected at colliders; no conjugate or momentum-polarized sector, no dark matter. A lead named by g2 and never assessed.

quotes.text: predicts the existence of a complete family of magnetically charged particles, as well as their neutral isotopic partners (all counterparts to the SM elementary particles)

findings.citation: D. Fryberger, "On Magneticons and some related matters", arXiv:1807.09606 (2018; arXiv preprint only)
findings.summary: Develops the magneticon, a magnetically charged spin-1/2 particle from a 'dyality' symmetry of classical electromagnetism, anticipates a full hadronic and leptonic spectrum of such particles, and suggests a second, magnetic photon accompanying them (two-potential formulation).
findings.difference: The second photon gives it the look of the separate-photon form, but the magnetic fermions live in ordinary space and are sought in collider data; no position/momentum structure, no dark matter in the abstract. PDF not parsable by WebFetch; read from the abstract.

quotes.text: (Actually, it is anticipated that there would be a full spectrum, both hadronic and leptonic, of such magnetically charged particles.)
Accompanying this spectrum of magnetic fermions, it is suggested that there may also be a second, or magnetic, photon.

findings.citation: J. Polchinski, "Monopoles, duality, and string theory", Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 19S1, 145 (2004), Dirac Centennial Symposium, arXiv:hep-th/0304042 (conference proceedings)
findings.summary: Proposes two 'principles of completeness': where charge is quantized, monopoles exist; and in a fully unified theory every gauge field has electric and magnetic sources with the minimal Dirac quantum. Adds that inflation has almost certainly diluted primordial monopoles beyond discovery.
findings.difference: Magnetic sources of the same gauge fields, in the same sector; the null result is laid to inflation. The modern form of C4's 'full magnetic counterpart' half (which #11 §11.2 gives as Montonen-Olive [T]), without a conjugate sector. Also a new finding of g3-magnetic-mirror/verify.json (written after known.json), same label.

quotes.text: In any fully unified theory, for every gauge field there will exist electric and magnetic sources
inflation has almost certainly diluted any primordial monopoles beyond discovery

findings.citation: V. Krasnoholovets, "Magnetic monopole as the shadow side of the electric charge", J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 1251, 012028 (2019), arXiv:2106.10225 (conference proceedings)
findings.summary: In the author's 'tessellattice' theory of space every electric charge turns periodically into a magnetic monopole over each de Broglie wavelength of its path; quarks likewise; the (anti)neutrino is 'the typical electron's monopole'.
findings.difference: Each charged particle has a magnetic counterpart, but as a periodic state of the same particle in ordinary space, tied to its de Broglie wavelength (its momentum), not a separate momentum-polarized analog; no dark matter; a framework outside mainstream physics.

quotes.text: a magnetic monopole appears as the tension state of the primary electric charge at its motion through each section of the path equal to the particle’s de Broglie wavelength
A (anti)neutrino emerges as the typical electron’s monopole.

findings.citation: S. Khademi, S. Nasiri, "Generalized gauge transformations in phase space picture of quantum mechanics: Kirkwood representation", J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 128, 012016 (2008), doi:10.1088/1742-6596/128/1/012016 (conference proceedings)
findings.summary: Generalizes gauge transformations from configuration space to phase space and finds that a general global gauge symmetry in phase space yields electric-charge quantization without Dirac's magnetic monopole, 'which is not detected yet'.
findings.difference: Gets from phase-space structure the charge quantization that the shared-photon form would get from magnetic analogs in the p-polarization (#11 §11.4), but does away with monopoles rather than placing them in momentum space; no dark matter. The same authors' 2009 talk 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?' could not be read (unverified leads).

quotes.text: It is shown that, the assumption of the general global gauge symmetry in phase space immediately yields the quantization of the electric charge.

findings.citation: M. A. Jafarizadeh, A. Rezaei-Aghdam, "T-duality in sigma models with Kaluza-Klein metric as electric-magnetic duality", Mod. Phys. Lett. A 14, 1497 (1999), arXiv:hep-th/9903154 (journal)
findings.summary: Shows that T-duality in sigma models with a Kaluza-Klein metric acts as electric-magnetic duality on some of their solitons, Buscher's transformation exchanging topological and Noether charges.
findings.difference: A bridge between a momentum-winding duality and electric-magnetic duality inside one theory, of the same kind as Harvey-Moore-Strominger (known); no second sector, no polarization of matter.

findings.citation: M. Born, "Reciprocity and the Number 137. Part I", Proc. R. Soc. Edinb. 59, 219 (1940), doi:10.1017/S037016460001230X (journal; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: Born reports Landé's argument that the reciprocity principle leads to a condition on the Planck constant whose value in units c = e = 1 is 137, that is, that reciprocity would fix the electromagnetic coupling, and reconsiders it.

findings.citation: C. A. Z. Vasconcellos, D. Hadjimichef, "CP Violation in Dual Dark Matter", Astron. Nachr. 335, 672 (2014), arXiv:1404.0409 (journal)
findings.summary: Extends electric-magnetic dual symmetry with a vector field C_mu as a dual partner of the photon and derives a 'dual dark matter' Lagrangian from the dual-symmetric one.

not_found.statement: No work proposes magnetic monopoles, or magnetically charged topological solitons, localized in momentum space or abundant in a momentum-polarized, conjugate or reciprocal sector, as matter or as dark matter. Searched beyond arXiv and INSPIRE: OpenAlex title/abstract (0 hits for "momentum space" AND monopole(s) AND dark matter/sector; 3 for phase space + magnetic charge + dark matter; all 253 records of "magnetic monopoles" AND "dark matter" read by title and filtered by abstract); DataCite (Zenodo, Figshare, OSF: 118 and 45 hits, all Berry-curvature physics or unrelated); Crossref posted content (Preprints.org, SSRN, OSF, Qeios, Research Square: 4 queries); WebSearch in English, Russian and Chinese and on viXra. Every monopole-dark-matter proposal found puts the monopoles in position space; every 'monopole in momentum space' is a Berry-curvature or bundle object (collisions: Majid-Schroers, Onoda-Tatara-Nagaosa).

No work explains the absence of observed monopoles by their being localized in momentum, or in a conjugate, reciprocal or dual space, rather than in position. The explanations found outside the known list use another time flow or universe (Henderson 2025, non-reviewed), a superposition of +-g with zero mean charge (Barut 1972), confinement inside every particle (Kursunoglu 1974), binding into monopole dimers (H. Liu 2026, Zenodo/Figshare, non-reviewed), or gravity forbidding monopoles (S. Maes 2020, OSF, non-reviewed). The one title that might state C3's argument, Khademi and Nasiri's 2009 talk 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?', could not be read (unverified leads).

No work places a magnetically charged counterpart of every electrically charged particle in a dual, conjugate, reciprocal or momentum-space sector. Full magnetic counterpart families appear only in ordinary space (Sullivan-Fryberger 2015, Fryberger 2018, Polchinski's completeness, Krasnoholovets 2019); a dark sector of magnetic charges under its own photon appears without any position-momentum structure (García-Moreno-Vento 2026, after Vento 2025); and works joining Born reciprocity, Fourier or T-duality to electric-magnetic duality do so formally, inside one theory (Jafarizadeh-Rezaei-Aghdam 1999, De Haro-Cinti 2025, Kriger 2026, the last excluding monopoles). No work combines S-duality and Born's rho to put the magnetic half of electromagnetism in the p-polarization (the shared-photon form).

Nasiri (Nasiry Ghidari), 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?', talk at the 'Multiphysics' conference, Lille University of Science and Technology, France, 9-11 December 2009 (University of Zanjan faculty listing, read by WebFetch); OpenAlex W3153563614 lists a 2009 item of that title in the Maltepe University open-access repository (hdl 20.500.12415/6128), no DOI, no abstract. The only title found that might state C3's argument.
unverified_leads.why_unverified: The repository returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and to curl (handle page and OAI endpoints); no proceedings or other copy found by four web searches. The g2 verifier's search-engine summary said it argues that phase-space uncertainty explains the null result; that is not verifiable. Inference, unverified: the same authors' 2008 paper (finding above) derives charge quantization from phase-space gauge symmetry without monopoles, so the talk may argue that monopoles are unnecessary rather than hidden in momentum space.

notes: Sweep beyond arXiv and INSPIRE for C2, C3 and C4. Tools: OpenAlex answered 10 distinct queries (oa01-oa06b, including a full read of the 253 OpenAlex records matching "magnetic monopoles" AND "dark matter" in title or abstract) before every request returned HTTP 429: OpenAlex's free daily budget, shared by every agent on this IP, was used up (resets at midnight UTC). OpenAlex offers a key in exchange for the user's email; not requested, since Paul has not agreed to send it. Cached OpenAlex results of other agents were scanned for monopole terms (nothing new). Semantic Scholar also returned 429. In their place: DataCite API (Zenodo, Figshare, OSF DOIs), Crossref posted-content filter (Preprints.org, SSRN, OSF, Research Square, Qeios, Cambridge Open Engage), Crossref journal search, WebSearch (extended; English, Russian, Chinese, viXra), WebFetch, and INSPIRE/arXiv for leads. Blocked: Maltepe repository, ResearchGate and Preprints.org (403), IOP PDF (bot check, not circumvented), Springer (login redirect). OpenAlex queries to re-run after the reset (not run): oa07-1..4 (null-result explanations; 'why/where/missing monopoles'; monopoles with parallel/mirror/shadow world; with extra dimensions), and fulltext "monopoles in momentum space" AND "dark matter"; fulltext "magnetic monopoles" AND "Born reciprocity"; title_and_abstract (electric-magnetic|electromagnetic duality) AND (position and momentum|Fourier transform|Born reciprocity|phase space); (magnetic counterpart|partner|analog) AND (every|each) AND charged particle; "dual electrodynamics" AND dark; "magnetic matter" AND "dark matter". Verdict: nothing anticipates C2, C3 or C4, and no new paper reaches partial except García-Moreno and Vento 2026, a continuation of a known partial. Six findings duplicate new findings of the round-1 verifiers (g2: Majid-Schroers, Onoda-Tatara-Nagaosa; g3: Polchinski, Born 1940, Vasconcellos-Hadjimichef, Qi et al.), whose verify.json files were written at 16:56-16:57, after known.json (16:54); they were re-verified independently here and the labels agree. The g3 verifier also has Born, Cheng and Green 1949 (recid:2012439), not re-read here. Checked and not reported: TGD (M. Pitkänen, blog posts of 19 and 30 May 2024, non-reviewed, no DOI or arXiv id): 'M8-H duality as an analog of momentum position duality for point-like particles replaced by 3-surface' and 'Monopole flux tubes carry heff>h phases of ordinary matter behaving like dark matter' (checked by WebFetch only) - dark matter on monopole flux tubes in space-time within a framework that has a momentum-position duality, at most related to C2; H. Liu 2026 (Zenodo/Figshare, monopole-antimonopole dimers as classical dark matter, explaining the null result by binding; position space, redundant with known monopolium papers); R. Kühne 2018 (Preprints.org; electric-magnetic duality likened to spin-mass duality, not position-momentum); S. Maes 2020 (OSF; gravity excludes monopoles); Lochak's leptonic monopole (AFLB; neutrino as its neutral state); Castelo Ferreira 2006 (hep-th/0601218; space-time coordinate duality maps electric to magnetic in 2+1 D, 'not related' to EM duality in 3+1 D); J.-K. Hwang 2020-21 (Preprints.org; bosons as magnetic monopoles); TOE-style Zenodo records. Cross-group leads (C1): Henderson 2025 (dark matter as five gravitationally coupled dual universes); R. Belfakih 2022, SSRN, doi:10.2139/ssrn.4065851 (dark matter as antimatter in a second space); A. A. Antonov 2019, J. Mod. Phys., doi:10.4236/jmp.2019.108067 ('invisible universes').
